children: Net profit reaches Rs 23,038 crore as net interest income grows 14.69 per cent; quarter includes a one-time gain from SBI Funds Management stake sale

State Bank of India (SBI) reported a 14.28 per cent year-on-year increase in standalone net profit to Rs 23,038 crore for the July-September quarter of FY27, supported by higher interest income and loan growth. Net interest income rose 14.69 per cent to Rs 49,143 crore in the quarter ended September 30, 2026.

The results, announced on Tuesday, also reflected an improvement in asset quality, with the gross non-performing asset (NPA) ratio declining to 1.39 per cent from 1.73 per cent a year earlier. However, the bank's net interest margin (NIM) for the entire banking business edged lower to 2.94 per cent from 2.96 per cent in the corresponding quarter last year.
Interest Income Drives Quarterly Performance

SBI's interest income increased 10.46 per cent year on year to Rs 1,32,019 crore in Q2 FY27, while interest expenses rose 8.09 per cent to Rs 82,876 crore. The difference between interest earned and interest paid lifted net interest income to Rs 49,143 crore, compared with Rs 42,847 crore in Q2 FY26.

Operating profit increased 7.28 per cent to Rs 34,226 crore from Rs 31,904 crore in the year-ago quarter. Total income grew 8.25 per cent to Rs 1,51,084 crore, while total expenses increased 8.54 per cent to Rs 1,16,859 crore.

Non-interest income declined 4.94 per cent to Rs 19,066 crore from Rs 20,056 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. Fee income, however, increased 9.63 per cent to Rs 9,549 crore, reflecting higher income from loan processing charges and other banking services.
SBI Funds Management Stake Sale Adds To Income

The bank's reported earnings included a one-time profit of Rs 7,288 crore from the sale of its stake in SBI Funds Management during Q2 FY27. In the corresponding quarter last year, the bank had recorded a one-time profit of Rs 4,593 crore from the sale of its stake in Yes Bank.

The difference in these one-time gains is an important factor in assessing the year-on-year movement in reported earnings. SBI's analyst presentation separately disclosed these items in its quarterly financial performance statement.
Advances Grow 17.84%, Deposits Rise 12.27%

SBI's gross advances increased 17.84 per cent year on year to Rs 52.08 lakh crore as of 30 September 2026. Total deposits grew 12.27 per cent to Rs 62.78 lakh crore during the same period. Domestic advances rose 16.94 per cent to Rs 43.77 lakh crore, while advances from foreign offices increased 22.86 per cent to Rs 8.31 lakh crore.

Retail personal loans, which accounted for 41.7 per cent of domestic advances, grew 14.54 per cent year on year. Small and medium enterprise (SME) advances increased 21.97 per cent, while agricultural advances grew 22.64 per cent. Corporate advances rose 16.12 per cent. On the deposit side, current account and savings account (CASA) deposits increased 8.13 per cent to Rs 22.97 lakh crore. Term deposits grew 14.26 per cent to Rs 36.98 lakh crore.
Net Interest Margin Improves Sequentially

SBI's whole-bank NIM stood at 2.94 per cent in Q2 FY27, against 2.96 per cent in Q2 FY26 and 2.86 per cent in the preceding quarter. Domestic NIM improved to 3.11 per cent from 3 per cent in Q1 FY27 and 3.08 per cent in the year-ago quarter. The bank reported an 11-basis-point sequential improvement in domestic NIM.

The improvement in domestic margins came as the domestic cost of deposits declined to 4.84 per cent in September 2026 from 5.04 per cent in March 2026. The domestic yield on advances stood at 8.22 per cent, compared with 8.50 per cent in March 2026.
Asset Quality Continues To Improve

SBI's gross NPA ratio declined to 1.39 per cent at the end of September 2026 from 1.73 per cent a year earlier and 1.47 per cent in June 2026. Gross NPAs fell to Rs 72,529 crore from Rs 76,243 crore in September 2025.

Net NPAs declined to 0.36 per cent from 0.42 per cent in the year-ago period. The net NPA amount stood at Rs 18,546 crore at the end of September 2026. Fresh slippages during Q2 FY27 stood at Rs 5,227 crore, compared with Rs 7,046 crore in the preceding quarter. Loan-loss provisions declined 33.23 per cent year on year to Rs 2,759 crore.
The bank's credit cost stood at 0.22 per cent for the quarter, compared with 0.39 per cent in Q2 FY26. Its provision coverage ratio, excluding accounts written off, stood at 74.43 per cent.
Capital Adequacy Strengthens

SBI's capital adequacy ratio (CRAR) improved to 16.09 per cent as of September 2026, against 14.62 per cent a year earlier. The common equity tier-1 (CET1) ratio stood at 13.34 per cent, compared with 11.47 per cent in September 2025. The bank's balance sheet expanded 12.88 per cent year on year to Rs 78.88 lakh crore at the end of September 2026, compared with Rs 69.87 lakh crore a year earlier.
